page: Amazon Web Services g6e.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, pairing dedicated x86_64 CPU resources with dedicated graphics and machine learning hardware. The server provides 16 virtual CPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, supported by 128 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz (8 GB per physical core). For accelerated execution, it includes a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace generation equipped with 45 GB of VRAM. Bundled local storage includes a 600 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional capability in machine learning acceleration. Across large language model inference tests, the NVIDIA L40S accelerator places the instance consistently in the top tier (top 10%) for both prompt processing and text generation across 135M, 7B, and 70B parameter models. CPU performance shows strong single-core throughput in stress-ng evaluations, ranking in the top 25%, while general Geekbench, PassMark, compression, and Redis operations hold steady within the average tier (middle 50%). Conversely, uncached large-block system memory bandwidth registers in the lower 25%, indicating that throughput-bound memory tasks outside the GPU memory space may experience architectural bottlenecks.

The hardware configuration provides high resource density for workloads demanding significant GPU memory alongside robust system host RAM and fast local scratch disk space. While uncached host memory operations present a tradeoff, the 45 GB GPU framebuffer and dedicated NVMe SSD minimize external storage latency. The instance is suited for AI inference deployments, deep learning model evaluation, graphics virtualization, 3D rendering pipelines, and data processing workflows requiring localized accelerator bandwidth.
